newsitem.title: UK: Thorn shares fall further on profits warning.
newsitem.headline: Thorn shares fall further on profits warning.

text.p: Stock in British rentals group Thorn Plc fell a further 10 pence to 155 pence on Monday, after chairman Sir Colin Southgate warned shareholders that sterling's strength would reduce current year profits by some 11 million stg.
Thorn shares were down in aggregate 22 pence or 12.43 percent by 1030 GMT. The stock opened some 10 pence lower after going ex-dividend today.
Southgate also told the group's annual meeting that its first quarter turnover was down by one percent on a constant currency basis and by 8.5 percent at actual rates.

Nick Bubb, an analyst at SocGen said, "the figures are a touch on the disappointing side in terms of UK trading and the foreign exchange hit. Our expectations were at 140 (million profit before tax) for the year and on the face of it that could be on the high side."

Southgate said revenue at the group's Radio Rentals UK television and video operation was down 8.9 percent on a year ago at the end of June. Terminations in the year to date are up by 20 percent versus last year following an increase in UK Insurance Premium Tax.
